newsitem.title: USA: NC Railroad lease may be terminated.
newsitem.headline: NC Railroad lease may be terminated.

text.p: Norfolk Southern Corp said it might terminate its operations on North Carolina Railroad Co lines if terms of its lease agreement to use the lines are not upheld by the federal Surface Transportation Board.

Norfolk Southern said it asked the board to prescribe the terms and conditions agreed to by Norfolk Southern and NC Rail directors and approved by NC Rail shareholders, but ruled invalid by a federal judge.
Norfolk Southern noted the judge ruled the NC Rail shareholders meeting invalid for lack of a quorum.

If the board responds favorably to an NC Rail request that the lease compensation be set at a level higher than agreed to, Norfolk Southern said, it would probably terminate its operations on parts or all of the NC Rail lines and reroute traffic to other routes.

Norfolk Southern pointed out that NC Rail's proxy materials advised its shareholders and the investment community that the guaranteed $8 million income stream in the extension agreement was the most attractive option available.

Responding to NC Rail's request that Norfolk Southern be directed to pay interim compensation of more than $680,000 per month pending final resolution of the question, Norfolk Southern suggested that the terms of the extension agreement be imposed, pointing out this would provide such compensation.

A less satisfactory alternative, Nofolk Southern said, would be for it to pay the amounts called for in the lease expired December 31, 1994. That would obligate Norfolk Southern to pay NC Rail about $600,000 a year in rental.

In connection with the approval of the extension by the NC Rail board of directors and, apparently, shareholders, Norfolk Southern said it made payments called for in the extension agreement totaling over $18 million.

"When shareholder approval was invalidated, Norfolk Southern was in the position of having paid $18 million to NCRR without a valid agreement, and where the old agreements would have required one-twentieth of that amount.

"Having 'overpaid' NCRR by over $17 million for the period of January 1, 1995, to July 15, 1996, Norfolk Southern felt it could not justify the payment of further rental unless its rights and obligations to NCRR were further clarified," the railroad said. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
